1.explanation: All these files define or test the existing number formatting logic for reports and templating: • report/handlebar-helpers-test.js validates the Handlebars helper that formats numbers. • report/formatter-test.js covers the top-level report formatter’s number output. • report/v2/renderer/format-helpers-test.js contains the core formatting utilities that should switch to toLocaleString. • report/v2/renderer/report-renderer-test.js and category-renderer-test.js verify that category scores and numeric metrics are rendered correctly. • report/v2/renderer/details-renderer-test.js checks detailed audit output (often numeric). Updating these files ensures that everywhere numbers appear in the generated report will use toLocaleString for consistent separators and precision.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show that when calling Number.prototype.toLocaleString with various maximumFractionDigits (and optional minimumFractionDigits) settings, we automatically get correct thousands separators and decimal precision without manual formatting. The goal is to replace all our ad-hoc number formatting (for metric values, element counts, diagnostics sizes, etc.) with toLocaleString to ensure consistency. The console snippet demonstrates cases like: 2445.8311.toLocaleString(undefined,{maximumFractionDigits:1}) → “2,445.8”, handling both thousands separators and rounding. We need to propagate this behavior throughout the report generator, Handlebars helpers, and any formatting utilities.
